analysis.title: Europe Open - Reboot pending
key_insights: Weak tech sentiment weighed on equities at the start of the week: Kospi -3.5%, Nasdaq futures -1.1%, Hang Seng +0.5% on short covering and rotation into laggards. The Asia desk says some selling may reflect funding for upcoming IPOs.
Citi's equity trading desk (CETS) says market risk/reward is incrementally better but it is not a dip buyer, because positioning-driven moves are unpredictable.

Nvidia earnings (Tuesday, after the US cash close) are the largest SPX event priced by options for the next month, at +/- 1.01%. FT reports ousted Nvidia CEO Huang is discussing a possible comeback, and Treasury Secretary Bessent said Nvidia needs a 'dramatic shakeup' in leadership.

Treasuries drifted with low conviction and lower volumes because of street-wide technical issues. Franchise flow saw better selling in the intermediates and the long end. Hawkish Fedspeak continued, with Schmid saying inflation is running too hot.

Dec Fed OIS pricing is about 27.5bp (Bloomberg WIRP), with 88bp priced into the curve by Sep 2027. Fed Chair Warsh speaks at 17:00 GMT at a labor market conference and any comment on monetary policy will be scrutinized, after Waller put a 50bp December hike on the table.

Japan Q3 GDP came in at -0.1% QoQ against 1.4% prior, and nominal GDP was 0.4%. Front-end JGB yields fell. Citi's macro strategist still expects a BoJ hike in December and stays paid front-BoJ meetings. BoJ's Takata argued for raising rates 'nimbly' rather than at a fixed pace and size.

USDJPY trades at 159.46, and 160 remains the key short-term barrier that has produced jitters every time it was tested. Interbank FX volumes in the Asia morning were 39% below the 30-day average. Franchise flows saw leveraged names buying USD, JPY and HKD and net selling EUR, GBP, AUD, NZD, CHF and THB.

Citi's Asia spot trader likes short AUDUSD and AUDJPY on softer China data. First support is 0.6750, and a break would open a test of the 200-week moving average at 0.6650-60. RBA November minutes and the October employment report are the key events this week.

Oil rallied after Iran struck an air base in Bahrain, the first direct strike since early September. Bahrain said it intercepted multiple Iranian aerial attacks. Iran's parliament speaker said the path to ending the conflict remains open if the US accepts Iran's 'logical conditions'.
A US-Russia-China trilateral meeting with Trump, Putin and Xi is confirmed for Thursday. Trump has said it would focus on denuclearization and that he also intends to discuss the Iran war.

China's October activity data was net soft. Retail sales slowed to 0.4% YoY, and the investment contraction deepened to -16.1% YoY, an all-time low outside Covid. Citi economists see growing downside risk to their 4.6% YoY forecast for 26Q4E and 2026E, and say the chance of more significant easing is rising.

Weekly Macro Brief from Citi's senior macro strategist: the case for selling USTs remains strong, with a growing bias toward UST steepeners. Value, inflation and fiscal policy point to higher UST yields. The Fed is behind the curve, which points to a steeper curve, higher inflation and most likely a weaker dollar.

Citi's strategist sees a BoE hike in December as increasingly likely and recommends staying paid front-BoE meetings and long back-end gilts cross-market. If odds rise that De Cos becomes the next ECB President, that would add dovish pricing to the front end of the EUR curve.

The week is heavy on headline risk: the APEC summit in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19 (Trump, Xi, possibly Putin), Nvidia earnings, FOMC minutes, about 20 Fedspeak events, UK jobs and inflation data ahead of the Dec MPC, and US and China retail earnings.
Canada October CPI is due at 13:30 GMT. Citi economists expect headline at 0.4% MoM (consensus 0.3%, prior 0.1%) and the house view is that the BoC holds in the near term.

German leader Merz said proposals for the top ECB jobs, including replacing Schnabel and Chief Economist Lane, will come this week. Citi economists expect Eurozone September industrial production at +0.7% MoM, above consensus.
earnings_insights: Nvidia reports Tuesday after the US cash close. Options price a +/- 1.01% SPX move from the event, the largest single-event SPX move priced for the next month. Citi's week-ahead cheatsheet says Nvidia 'should beat' (forecast, not a print), while leadership questions should persist.
Major US and China retailers also report this week (no names or figures given).

tension_points.bull_case: Citi's macro strategist argues the Fed is behind the curve and will stay there, pointing to higher inflation, a steeper curve and a weaker dollar, with UST sales favoured.
tension_points.bear_case: Hawkish Fedspeak (Schmid: inflation 'running too hot') and Waller's 50bp December hike remark are driving the repricing. Dec OIS pricing is only about 27.5bp, so a hike is not fully priced.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Warsh remarks at 17:00 GMT that do not endorse a hike would test the repricing.
